Thanks for looping me in — tagging a short packaging playbook so uploads aren’t back-and-forth: 

File naming conventions (required):
- <EVID-###>_<ShortDesc>_<YYYYMMDD>.pdf (examples below)
- Manifest: SIG_Package_<Customer>_<YYYYMMDD>_manifest.txt

Minimum evidence set we should include (recommended order):
1) EVID-001_SOC2_TypeII_Redacted.pdf — SOC 2 report (redact client-specific customer names if present)
2) EVID-002_ArchDiagram.pdf — high-level architecture (public-facing and internal zones)
3) EVID-003_DataFlow.pdf — data flow with in/out of Redwood systems, storage location notes
4) EVID-004_KMS_encryption_summary.pdf — KMS description, key rotation cadence, CMEK notes if in Private deployments
5) EVID-005_SSO_SAML_metadata.pdf — SSO config screenshots (MFA enabled checkbox + last login sample)
6) EVID-006_Subprocessors_list.csv — subprocessors + regions + links to SOCs
7) EVID-007_Config_Mgmt_Screenshots.pdf — limited screenshots of infrastructure as code pipelines (avoid secrets)
8) EVID-008_Retention_Policy.pdf

Packaging notes:
- OneTrust limit: split any PDF >28MB into logical parts (e.g., SOC exhibits separated). Flatten PDFs and embed fonts; avoid Javascript in PDFs.
- Add an evidence-index CSV (we use evidence-index-template.csv) mapping SIG question IDs to EVID-### file names and page ranges where relevant. OneTrust supports per-question attachments; the CSV helps their intake team.
- For sensitive logs/screenshots, provide redacted versions; mark originals as "available on request under NDA/airgap".
- Use EVID tags inside the SIG answers PDF next to answers (e.g., “(see EVID-003)”) to make mapping trivial.

I’m attaching the evidence-index-template.csv we use internally. Neha — can you assemble the initial PDFs and the mapping? Karthik — I’ll review and sign off before upload.

Marissa Cole
